poke_evidence.recorded process 1885744 (score 2): write 0 -> P2 digit rect 46 bar px => 2 px (blank); write 1 -> 24 px / 1 bar; write 2 -> 46 px / 2 bars; read-back confirmed every write; ping ok; restored 2
poke_evidence.second process 1979883 (score 1): baseline 24 px / 1 bar; write 0 -> 2 px (blank); write 1 -> 24 px; ping ok; restored 1
poke_evidence.glyph7: write 7 (and 3,4,100) renders the SAME tally as the score already displayed (46 px = 2 bars in the score-2 process, 24 px = 1 bar in the score-1 process): the READY tally is capped by the number of rounds played / the glyph set has no >2 form, so a distinct glyph for 7 cannot be produced. 0<->blank and 1<->one bar are exact.

score.cap_note: The READY tally is one bar per win capped by the number of rounds already played: in a process that had played 1 round, poking 2 drew 1 bar; after a 2nd round, poking 2/7 drew 2 bars. So the field is the wins value the HUD draws, but the HUD has no distinct >2 rendering - a 7 glyph cannot be produced by design.
score.allocation_note: 0xd5f57c8 is the wins cell once a round/match has been played (both recorded processes, mined independently, land on the same absolute address in the fixed-base 0xd412000 region). At a brand-new READY with no round played, that offset is not yet the wins cell (a poke there crashed one process). So: stable and safe to use after the first round, not a static global from process start.

phase.note: 2283 u32 slots are constant in all 7 READY dumps, constant in all 5 LIVE dumps, and constant again in the 3 post-round READY dumps (a != b). 1583 of them are in the new regions. The clean 0/1 and 0/3 cells were poked both ways: 15 clean candidates poked to 0 inside a live round (no round end, no wall, no HUD, ping ok, restored), and 8 poked to 1 at READY (no match start). None is the phase driver; the phase is either not the field I tested or is not consulted while the state machine is already running.

neighbours.value: 0 (not the P1 counter: poking 1 leaves the YELLOW rect blank)

crash_log: pid 1885744: writing float 1.0f (0x3F800000) to the score 0xd5f57c8 at READY killed the process within 0.5 s (the int writes 0/1/2/7/100 were all safe). The renderer evidently indexes a glyph sprite/frame by the raw int.

pid 1967166: writing u32 2 to 0xd5f57c8 at a FRESH READY, before any round had been played, killed the process; poking 1 there did not redraw the tally either. Interpretation: the wins cell is allocated when the round/match state exists - at a fresh READY that offset still belongs to another allocation, and writing into it corrupted that object. In both recorded processes (1885744, 1979883) the wins counter is at 0xd5f57c8 once a round has been played, and the pokes are safe and visible.
dead_ends: 25 u32 candidates inside the old 15-region set (worker Z) were all display-unrelated; the score is indeed only in the newly dumped regions (0xd412000 / 0xece0000).

The other 3 interval survivors (0xf3c6368/0xf3c63e8/0xf3c6468, 0x80-stride records in 0xece0000) track 0->1->2 but poking 0 at them does not change the HUD: copies/related counters, not the displayed value.

The P1 (YELLOW) wins counter was NOT found: it stays 0 through this session, so the 0->1 interval signature cannot see it. The candidates adjacent to 0xd5f57c8 (+4, +8, +0x38) do not drive the YELLOW rect.

Writing x into a live fighter body (0x1902800 +0xEC / +0xFC) is overwritten within one tick: the game recomputes the body position, so teleporting a fighter to the goal is not possible with a plain write. This is why the round was won by forfeit instead.
The READY tally is not a decimal digit but one bar per win, capped by the rounds already played; a '7' poke therefore cannot produce a distinct glyph in the tally cell.
Long idle LIVE windows are stable (35 s, no round end), so the READY->LIVE field (phase) needs a behavioural poke; the 0/1 candidate list (2283 total) was not narrowed enough in the remaining budget.
